channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakh Journalist's Widow Details Transnational Repression and Husband's Murder Investigation
item.description: Natalia Sadykova, widow of slain Kazakh journalist Aidos Sadykov, spoke at the OSCE about ongoing persecution after her husband's murder. She detailed diplomatic espionage, alleged judicial obstruction by Kazakh oligarchs in Ukraine, and digital censorship. Sadykova highlighted the two-year delay in justice and the transnational nature of authoritarian repression.

item.title: Uzbek State Sells 49.07% Stake in Uzbek-Chinese Joint Venture UzXCMG
item.description: Uzbekistan's state is selling its 49.07% share in the UzXCMG joint venture, located in Urgench, Khorezm region. The company specializes in mining and underground work equipment. The starting price is 140.53 billion soums, with a deposit of 4.22 billion soums. The auction is scheduled for October 19.

item.title: Uzbek President to Attend CICA Summit in Baku
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Azerbaijan on October 14-15 for the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA). The summit, hosted by Azerbaijan, will focus on strengthening trust, peace, and security in Asia, and institutional development. Discussions will cover transport connectivity, digitalization, and economic growth. Bilateral meetings are also planned.

item.title: 5.5 Million Hectares of Pasture Land Allocated to Rural Residents
item.description: In Kazakhstan, 5.5 million hectares of land have been allocated for public pasture use as part of efforts to return and redistribute agricultural lands. This initiative aims to address pasture shortages, reducing the deficit from 8 million to 3 million hectares. The vice-minister of agriculture stated that 13 million hectares have been returned to the state overall.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Annual Heating Tariff Increase Up to 10%
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering a proposal to increase centralized heating tariffs annually by up to 10%, starting from 2028, adjusted for inflation. The Ministry of Construction and Housing-Communal Services drafted the proposal. This follows a presidential decision to gradually bring heating tariffs to cost-recovery levels by 2030. Separate increases for heating and hot water are also planned from November 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers "Green" Technologies for Greenhouse Farming to Reduce Emissions
item.description: Uzbekistan is exploring the implementation of "green" technologies in greenhouse operations to ensure environmentally safe practices. A presentation to President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed the state of greenhouses in Tashkent and surrounding areas. The proposal includes a special ecological regime for greenhouses, prioritizing natural gas, electricity, geothermal, and solar energy, while restricting the burning of harmful materials.

item.title: Customs Regime Facilitates Export Growth in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing measures to expand production and support exports. The 'Processing within Customs Territory' regime exempts VAT, excise tax, and duties, boosting export potential. In Navoiy region, raw materials worth over $22.9 million were imported for processing in early 2026, benefiting companies like 'Solis Olis'.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces Special Tax Regimes for Self-Employed, Businesses, and Farmers
item.description: Kazakhstan has introduced special tax regimes to help entrepreneurs optimize their tax obligations. Self-employed individuals will pay 4% for social purposes. Businesses using simplified declarations will have a base rate of 4%, adjustable by local authorities. Farmers will pay a 0.5% individual income tax. These measures aim to create favorable conditions for entrepreneurship.

item.title: Erdogan Pledges Turkish Support to Saudi Arabia in Conflict Against Houthis
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has assured Saudi Arabia of Turkey's support in its conflict with the Houthis. During a phone call with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Erdogan condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi territory. He expressed confidence in Saudi Arabia's ability to overcome these difficult times, following recent deadly Houthi assaults on Riyadh's international airport.

item.title: Trump Suggests Iran Directed Recent Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump suggested that Iran likely directed the recent Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, describing them as 'very ugly.' He speculated that the Houthis might be attempting to raise oil prices before the US midterm elections. Trump stated he would not forget this situation, even after leaving office.

item.title: Zelensky Says Western Allies Did Not Warn Ukraine of Russian Missile Strikes on Kyiv
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Western partners did not provide advance intelligence regarding Russia's missile attack on Kyiv on October 12th. Air raid sirens reportedly sounded only after the initial explosions. Zelensky indicated that no prior warning was received from allies about the five ballistic missiles launched by Russia.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy Ministry Addresses Gas Pipeline Explosion in Russia
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy has commented on the gas pipeline explosion in Russia's Penza region. The ministry stated that gas supply from Russia to Kazakhstan continues normally under existing contracts. Transit of gas to Uzbekistan via Kazakhstan is also proceeding as planned. Kazakhstan's gas transportation system is operating without deviations.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Healthcare System Received 1.9 Trillion Tenge Through Social Health Insurance Fund
item.description: Kazakhstan's hospitals and clinics received 1.933 trillion tenge over nine months of 2026 via the Social Health Insurance Fund. Finance Minister Madi Takiev stated these funds were transferred from the republican budget to the fund, which then disbursed them to medical organizations. An information system, Qalqan, now integrates payments.

item.title: Uzbekistan Adopts German Experience in Inclusive Education for Children with Special Needs
item.description: Uzbekistan is adopting German experience in inclusive education for children with special needs. Seminars were held with specialists from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich for hospital school teachers. Participants studied German practices for educating long-term hospitalized children and creating inclusive environments for those with autism and behavioral disorders.

item.title: Funds for Maslikhat Elections in Kazakhstan to be Allocated from Government Reserve
item.description: Funds for the upcoming maslikhat (local assembly) elections in Kazakhstan will be allocated from the government's reserve fund. Central Election Commission member Mikhail Bortnik stated that estimates will be submitted to the government. Approximately 75-80% of the costs will cover election commission members' payments.

item.title: UN Launches Disaster Protection Projects in Afghanistan's Baghlan Province
item.description: The UN Development Programme is implementing flood protection infrastructure in Baghlan Province through the PAIDAAR project to safeguard homes and agricultural land. Funded by the Special Trust Fund for Afghanistan, the initiative aims to reduce flood risks and enhance community resilience following devastating 2024 floods. This effort supports disaster preparedness and risk reduction.

item.title: IOM Reports 112 Disaster Risk Reduction Projects Implemented in Afghanistan Since 2025
item.description: The International Organization for Migration has completed 112 projects across Afghanistan aimed at reducing natural disaster risks since 2025. The organization emphasizes that preparedness and early action are crucial for strengthening resilience in vulnerable areas. These initiatives have also enhanced local capacities in preparedness, coordination, and technical skills.

item.title: Kazakhstan Mandates Minimum Share of Domestic Products in Retail Stores from October 20
item.description: Starting October 20, Kazakhstan will implement a new requirement for retail chains to ensure a minimum share of domestic products across all product categories. The Minister of Trade and Integration, Arman Shakkaliyev, announced that 72 memorandums have been signed with retail chains to promote Kazakhstani goods. Overall trade volume in the country increased by 16% in the first nine months.

item.title: Atyrau Region Blocks Nearly 3,000 Websites and Fraudulent Advertisements
item.description: Authorities in Kazakhstan's Atyrau region have blocked approximately 3,000 phishing websites and fake advertisements using the 'Cybercontrol' program. The 'Antifraud Center' system also recovered over 21.2 million tenge from victims. Since the start of the year, 484 fraud cases have been registered, with 126 solved and 38 individuals identified.

item.title: Former Boyfriend Sentenced to 14 Years for Stabbing Death of 20-Year-Old Woman in Abai Region
item.description: A court in Semey has sentenced a young man to 14 years in prison for the brutal stabbing murder of 20-year-old Dilnaz Zhumagulova in Kazakhstan's Abai region. Her body was found on July 13. The court also partially granted the victim's parents' civil claim, ordering the defendant to pay 20 million tenge for moral damages.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enhances Pediatric Oncology Care with International Collaboration and Research
item.description: Uzbekistan is expanding international scientific research and cooperation in pediatric oncology as part of its National Plan for 2025-2035. Collaborations with WHO, St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, and the Medical University of Vienna aim to implement advanced diagnostic and treatment methods. Over 200 specialists are slated for training and international internships by 2030.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces New Financial Mechanisms to Support Entrepreneurs
item.description: Kazakhstan has implemented new financial support mechanisms for entrepreneurs, including the 'Orleu' program, a special guarantee fund with second-tier banks, and mobile support centers in regions. These measures aim to boost entrepreneurial activity and create favorable conditions for domestic production, as stated by Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Increase Heating and Hot Water Tariffs Starting November 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan is planning to raise heating and hot water tariffs for the population starting November 1, 2026. The Ministry of Construction and Housing and Communal Services has proposed new tariffs, aiming to gradually align them with service costs by 2030. In Tashkent, tariffs are expected to increase by 30%.

item.title: Kazakhstan Continues Discussions on Establishing Its Own Automotive Brand
item.description: Kazakhstan is still exploring the possibility of creating its own automotive brand and is in negotiations with foreign car manufacturers. The Vice Minister of Industry and Construction stated that the initiative requires careful evaluation, considering existing market competition. Specific launch details remain premature.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister Discusses Bilateral Relations with Qatar's Ambassador
item.description: Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi met with Qatar's ambassador to Afghanistan, Mardef Al-Qashouti, in Kabul. They discussed bilateral relations and Qatar's role in facilitating the Taliban's international engagement. Muttaqi noted expanding international relations, while Qatar's ambassador reaffirmed commitment to strengthening these ties.

item.title: Kazakhstan Announces Future Salary Increases for Public Sector Employees
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of National Economy, Serik Zhumangarin, outlined plans for public sector salary increases. Since January 1, 2024, average salaries rose 1.9 times, with lower-paid staff seeing a 2.2 times increase. Further 16% raises are planned for low-paid staff from January 1, 2025. Future increases are expected every three years.

item.title: Kazakhstan Citizens Withdraw 490 Billion Tenge Early from Pension Fund
item.description: Kazakh citizens have withdrawn 490 billion tenge in early pension savings withdrawals since the start of the year. The majority, 404 billion tenge, was withdrawn in the first half before minimum thresholds increased. Pension assets grew by 6.1% to 26.6 trillion tenge.

item.title: Putin Expresses Concern Over Declining Russian Culture in Central Asia at CIS Summit
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin voiced concerns at the CIS summit in Turkmenistan about the erosion of Russian culture and influence across member states. Despite the organization's history of inactivity, Putin promoted the CIS as a vehicle to maintain cultural and historical ties in Central Asia and the South Caucasus, highlighting a fear of losing cultural dominance.

item.title: Uzbekistan Marks 35 Years of Independence, Emphasizing Human Dignity as Development Basis
item.description: Uzbekistan celebrated its 35th anniversary of independence, with President Shavkat Mirziyoyev outlining strategic priorities for the next decade. The country has undergone significant transformations, prioritizing national values, historical memory, economic opportunities, and human interests. The principle of 'For the sake of human honor and dignity' guides reforms, aiming to protect citizens' rights and improve living conditions.

item.title: Kazakh Minister Explains Discrepancy in Economic Growth Forecasts
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy, Serik Zhumangarin, explained the significant difference between government and National Bank economic growth forecasts. He cited changing external and internal conditions, including an oil production shortfall and currency appreciation, as reasons for the divergence.

item.title: Firearms Used in Altercation in Zharkent, Kazakhstan; Criminal Case Opened
item.description: A criminal case is being investigated following an incident in Zharkent, Kazakhstan, where firearms were used during an altercation between men. Police have initiated cases for hooliganism and attempted murder. One 33-year-old man was hospitalized with gunshot wounds. Authorities have confiscated a weapon and arrested two suspects.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belgium Leaders Discuss AI's Impact on Higher Education at Forum
item.description: The Rector's Forum, attended by leaders of Kazakh and Belgian higher education institutions, convened at the Alem.ai international center. Discussions focused on the impact of artificial intelligence on education and scientific research. Participants explored Kazakhstan's role as a regional hub and the integration of AI in academic and educational processes. Several agreements were signed to expand partnerships.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Finance Ministry Assures Tax System Resilience Amid Russian Service Disruptions
item.description: Kazakhstan's Finance Minister Madi Takiev stated that the national tax reporting system operates on the ministry's own servers and databases, with backups in place. He confirmed that taxpayers do not use systems like 1C-Accounting for state settlements. This assurance follows disruptions to Russian services like Yandex Go, which affected some taxi and delivery components operating outside Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Maslikhat Elections May Cost More Than Kurultai Elections, Says CEC Member
item.description: A member of Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission (CEC), Mikhail Bortnik, explained that elections for maslikhats (local representative bodies) could be more expensive than Kurultai elections. This is due to the involvement of 3,022 district election commissions. Funds for these extraordinary elections will be allocated from the government's reserve budget, as they were not initially included in the Republic of Kazakhstan's budget.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Deputy PM Defends Tax Reform Amid Budget Shortfall Concerns
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin stated the tax reform has met expectations, generating 3 trillion tenge in additional budget revenue over nine months. Despite a VAT shortfall, he argued the reform is the economy's sole cash source and performing well, projecting at least 3.6 trillion tenge by year-end.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economic Growth to Outpace China and India by 2026, UN Forecasts
item.description: The UN forecasts that Kyrgyzstan's economy will grow by 8.8% in 2026, surpassing the growth rates of China and India. This projected expansion is expected to position Kyrgyzstan among the fastest-developing economies in the region. The forecast highlights significant economic momentum for the Central Asian nation.

item.title: Former Military Officer's Body Found in Helmand After Five Months
item.description: The body of a former military officer, Allah Dad Badizai, was found in Helmand province five months after his arrest by Taliban intelligence. Sources reported that the Taliban initially denied arresting him but later handed his body over to his family. This incident occurs amidst ongoing human rights violations against former government personnel.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev to Visit Azerbaijan for CICA Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will pay a working visit to Azerbaijan on October 14-15. He will participate in the seventh summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku.

item.title: Tajikistan's Fall Conscription Plan Achieves 84% Fulfillment in Ten Days
item.description: In the first ten days of the fall conscription for Tajikistan's Armed Forces, the recruitment plan reached 84% completion. The Ministry of Defense reported on October 12 that over 40 cities and districts had fully met their fall conscription targets ahead of schedule. Previously, the ministry had announced 55% of the plan was fulfilled on the first day.

item.title: Uzbek President to Attend CICA Summit in Baku for Working Visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Azerbaijan on October 14-15 for a working trip. He will participate in the 7th summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku. The summit agenda includes strengthening confidence, ensuring peace and security in Asia, and institutional development of CICA. Bilateral meetings with foreign leaders are also planned.
